answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable deposit that grows with the number of identities it claims, like tending a grove where every new tree costs water. Peers then mirror each other's behaviour records: an identity that never delivers useful work earns no endorsements, so its deposit stays locked while honest agents harvest rewards like an orchard in season. Cloning thousands of fake agents becomes a money pit, because each clone pays the same deposit yet cannot fake a history of real service.
